chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What is the expected major product when (R)-2-Bromobutane is treated with Sodium cyanide (NaCN) in DMSO?
questions.explanation: Treating (R)-2-Bromobutane with Sodium cyanide (NaCN) in DMSO yields (S)-2-Methylbutanenitrile + NaBr. Rationale: Cyanide undergoes backside SN2 attack in a polar aprotic solvent, inverting the chiral center.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 1-Bromopropane into 1-Azidopropane + NaBr?
questions.explanation: To convert 1-Bromopropane into 1-Azidopropane + NaBr, the appropriate reagent is Sodium azide (NaN3) in DMF. Rationale: Azide ion acts as an excellent unhindered nucleophile to displace primary bromide rapidly.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane is treated with Water / acetone (room temp)?
questions.explanation: Treating 2-Bromo-2-methylpropane with Water / acetone (room temp) yields tert-Butanol ((CH3)3COH) + HBr. Rationale: Rate-determining ionization to tertiary carbocation followed by rapid water capture and deprotonation.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of (S)-3-Bromo-3-methylhexane into (±)-3-Methoxy-3-methylhexane (racemic mixture)?
questions.explanation: To convert (S)-3-Bromo-3-methylhexane into (±)-3-Methoxy-3-methylhexane (racemic mixture), the appropriate reagent is Methanol (CH3OH). Rationale: Solvolysis proceeds through a planar achiral carbocation, attacked with equal probability from top and bottom.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 2-Bromobutane is treated with Sodium ethoxide (NaOEt) in ethanol / heat?
questions.explanation: Treating 2-Bromobutane with Sodium ethoxide (NaOEt) in ethanol / heat yields trans-2-Butene (major) + cis-2-Butene + 1-Butene. Rationale: Small unhindered ethoxide base abstracts beta-proton to yield the more substituted, thermodynamic alkene.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Which reagent or set of reaction conditions will best accomplish the transformation of 2-Bromobutane into 1-Butene (major)?
questions.explanation: To convert 2-Bromobutane into 1-Butene (major), the appropriate reagent is Potassium tert-butoxide (t-BuOK) in t-BuOH / heat. Rationale: Bulky tert-butoxide base abstracts the sterically more accessible primary beta-proton.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Sodium ethoxide (NaOEt) / heat to yield 3-Methylcyclohexene (exclusive elimination product) as the major product?
questions.explanation: trans-1-Bromo-2-methylcyclohexane reacts with Sodium ethoxide (NaOEt) / heat to yield 3-Methylcyclohexene (exclusive elimination product). Rationale: The axial bromine can only achieve anti-periplanar alignment with the axial C3 hydrogen, not the C2 hydrogen.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 2-Chloro-2-methylbutane is treated with Ethanol (heat, no strong base)?
questions.explanation: Treating 2-Chloro-2-methylbutane with Ethanol (heat, no strong base) yields 2-Methyl-2-butene (major) + 2-Methyl-1-butene. Rationale: Ionization forms a 3° carbocation; weak solvent base removes a proton to yield the Zaitsev alkene.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: Which starting material will react with Sodium methanethiolate (NaSCH3) in DMSO to yield (R)-sec-Butyl methyl sulfide as the major product?
questions.explanation: (S)-2-Butyl tosylate reacts with Sodium methanethiolate (NaSCH3) in DMSO to yield (R)-sec-Butyl methyl sulfide. Rationale: Methanethiolate attacks the electrophilic carbon with inversion, displacing the excellent tosylate leaving group.

questions.chapter_title: Reactions of Alkyl Halides: Nucleophilic Substitutions and Eliminations
questions.question: What is the expected major product when 3-Hydroxybutanal (aldol) is treated with Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) / heat?
questions.explanation: Treating 3-Hydroxybutanal (aldol) with Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) / heat yields 2-Butenal (crotonaldehyde) + H2O. Rationale: Strong base deprotonates the acidic alpha-carbon forming an enolate that expels hydroxide leaving group.
